headline: A global bond sell-off sends US yields to 24-year highs and oil back above $100; the first nuclear clocks tick in Vienna and Beijing; the EU agrees its biggest Russia sanctions list.

stories.title: Global bond sell-off: US 10- and 30-year yields hit 24-year highs, French debt under pressure, oil back above $100
facts: US 10-year Treasury yield rose more than 8bp to about 5.356%, its highest since April 2002; the 30-year reached about 5.725%, highest since May 2002 (Quartz).
Stocks slid a day after record closes: Dow −451 points (−0.9%), S&P 500 −0.6%, Nasdaq −0.9%. Europe’s Stoxx 600 fell 1%, Italy’s FTSE MIB nearly 2.5%.
NBC: French and Italian bond yields were heading for their biggest one-day jump since March, and the UK 30-year gilt yield hit its highest since 1998.
Brent traded back above $101 a barrel. Yahoo Finance cites UK officials reporting at least nine attacks in the Strait of Hormuz so far in October, plus a storm heading for the Gulf Coast.

IMF chief Georgieva told France to “get your house in order”: French 10-year yields are up more than 100bp this year and now exceed Italy’s. WSJ reports Paris is weighing more short-term debt issuance.
Still to come: a $39bn 10-year Treasury auction and minutes from the Fed’s September meeting, where it raised rates for the first time since 2023.
stories.whyItMatters: This is the cost of the Iran-war energy shock moving into government borrowing costs. Higher long-term yields feed into mortgages, corporate debt and budgets, including the German and French ones.

stories.title: The first nuclear clocks are ticking, in Vienna and Beijing
facts: Two teams published in Nature: TU Wien in Vienna and a Tsinghua-led group in Beijing. Both keep time with thorium-229 nuclei embedded in crystals, using the atomic nucleus instead of electrons as in atomic clocks.

Both prototypes drift by only a few millionths of a second per year. That is still several orders of magnitude worse than today’s best atomic clocks, but this is the very first generation (Welt der Physik).

SCMP: the Beijing clock is about six times as stable, and two separately grown crystals kept the same time, a sign the clocks can be reproduced. Vienna used its clock to look for dark matter and found none.
RND’s headline credits Braunschweig’s PTB with the breakthrough: a thorium clock running stably for more than 24 hours.
stories.whyItMatters: Nuclear clocks could eventually beat atomic clocks and test whether the constants of nature really are constant. Braunschweig’s national metrology institute, the PTB, is part of the story.

image.alt: Crystal holder of the thorium nuclear clock at TU Wien

stories.title: EU ambassadors agree the largest-ever Russia sanctions list: 1,646 names
facts: Agreed unanimously in Brussels on Wednesday: 743 individuals and 826 entities tied to Russia’s war effort, plus 77 lawmakers who ran in occupied Ukraine in September’s Duma vote (Euronews).
Targets span Russia’s defence industry, from shipyards and aviation firms to electronics makers, armoured-vehicle repair shops and aerospace companies (Kyiv Independent).
Foreign ministers formally adopt it on Monday 12 Oct in Luxembourg, when the names are published. It means travel bans, asset freezes and funding bans.
The blacklist will then cover almost 4,650 names. After this, the EU plans smaller rolling listings; work on listings over the Leipzig airport drone incident has already started.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows unity after last month’s fight over delisting Usmanov and Fridman, but sanctions still need unanimity, and the plan to switch to majority voting needs unanimity too.

image.alt: Vladimir Putin at a table with uniformed Russian military officers

stories.title: Musk: Grok Bot will route tasks to rival models too, including Claude Opus 5.5, Midjourney and Suno
facts: Musk on X: “@SpaceX will use the best back end model for any given task, including Claude Opus 5.5, MidJourney, Suno and other leading APIs.”
In a follow-up post he said simple questions go to small, fast models and complex ones to large models. He did not say which jobs go to which outside provider (TNW).
TNW: the change came a day after users reported trouble reaching Grok on mobile and web; SpaceXAI gave no official cause.
City AM calls it a notable U-turn after billions spent on xAI’s own models, and a commercial boost for Anthropic ahead of its planned listing.
stories.whyItMatters: Agent products are turning into routers that pick a model per task, which makes the model behind the brand matter less than the routing.

stories.title: Nadella and Huang unveil the Surface Laptop Ultra on Nvidia’s RTX Spark chip, built to run AI locally
facts: Unveiled together by Microsoft’s Satya Nadella and Nvidia’s Jensen Huang at Wednesday’s Windows and Surface event in San Francisco (Quartz).
RTX Spark is Nvidia’s first main processor for Windows PCs: a Blackwell GPU fused with a MediaTek-designed Arm CPU (N1X), up to 128GB unified memory and 1 petaflop of AI compute.
The laptop has a 15-inch mini-LED display, Microsoft’s biggest trackpad yet, USB-C, USB-A and a full-size SD reader.
They are also building agent-security tooling: new Windows protections and an Nvidia runtime, OpenShell, that controls what agents can access and where queries go.
Price is the open question. Memory costs are pushing AI hardware up, and Nvidia recently raised its DGX Spark desktop about 75% to $6,950.
stories.whyItMatters: Microsoft wants part of the AI workload off Azure and onto Windows PCs, and Nvidia gets into laptops as the main chip, not just the graphics card.

image.alt: Microsoft logo on a phone screen in front of an Nvidia logo

stories.title: Google opens Playground, a prompt-to-game maker, and a public SynthID checker for AI media
facts: Playground (Google Labs): describe a game in text, pick 2D/3D and single- or multiplayer, then share it by link or publish it to a gallery with leaderboards. Unity Spark integration is coming later.
It starts US-only for 18+. Playing is free; creating uses weekly tokens, with higher limits for Google One AI subscribers (TechCrunch).
SynthID.com lets anyone check images, video and audio for AI watermarks, now including those from partners OpenAI, Nvidia, Kakao and soon Apple (Ars Technica).
You need a Google, OpenAI or Apple login, and the quota is about 10 checks a day, to stop people tuning watermark-removal tools. Google says it gets 1 million verification requests a day.
Limits: Meta uses its own watermark, and open-weight models often use none, so a clean result does not mean a file is real.
stories.whyItMatters: Google is making it easier to create media and to check it on the same day; the checker only catches watermarks from companies that opt in.

stories.title: Ryanair pulls out of Bremen from April 2027 over airport fees and cuts 12 routes in Vienna
facts: Bremen loses about 400,000 passengers a year, more than a fifth of its traffic. Ryanair had paid the city roughly €3M a year (n-tv, airliners.de).
Economy senator Kristina Vogt (Linke): Ryanair wanted the airport’s services “almost free of charge”. Meeting its demands would have cost about €4M more a year and broken state-aid rules.
Ryanair has already cut back in Hamburg and Berlin over fees and is shifting to smaller airports, where Bremen says state-aid rules are looser.
In Vienna it removes four based aircraft and 12 routes this winter, affecting 80 jobs. O’Leary blames Austria’s €12 ticket tax and threatens more cuts.
stories.whyItMatters: Low-cost flying in Germany keeps shrinking toward subsidised regional airports. For Bremen, an airport already being restructured, the gap is hard to fill.

image.alt: A Ryanair Boeing 737 on an airport taxiway

stories.title: Five ex-Barclays traders have their Libor/Euribor rate-rigging convictions quashed
facts: The Court of Appeal in London overturned the convictions of Jay Merchant, Jonathan Mathew, Philippe Moryoussef, Alex Pabon and Colin Bermingham on Wednesday (BBC).
Four had served jail terms; Moryoussef was sentenced in his absence in 2018 after France refused to extradite him.
It follows two other traders’ convictions being overturned last year. Full reasons are due later; 19 City traders were convicted across nine trials in the UK and US from 2015 to 2019.
Merchant says he wants “those responsible for what happened” held accountable.
stories.whyItMatters: One of the signature prosecutions of the post-2008 era keeps falling apart, which puts pressure on the UK Serious Fraud Office.

image.alt: The Royal Courts of Justice in London

stories.title: Tropical Storm Isaias heads for the US Gulf Coast as a likely Cat 2 hurricane, the season’s latest first hurricane since 1905
facts: Formed Wednesday off eastern Mexico; the NHC expects rapid strengthening into a strong Category 2 before landfall between eastern Louisiana and the western Florida Panhandle (Guardian).
The Atlantic season’s first hurricane has not formed this late since 8 October 1905; a strong El Niño had kept the Atlantic quiet.
A hurricane watch covers Gulf, Bay, Walton and Okaloosa counties in Northwest Florida; landfall is expected Friday or Saturday, with storm surge, flash flooding and possible tornadoes (WJHG).
Chevron is evacuating non-essential staff from offshore platforms, which adds to the oil spike (Yahoo Finance).

image.alt: Satellite image of Tropical Storm Isaias over the Gulf of Mexico

facts.text: The Bundestag transport committee backed the Hannover–Hamburg high-speed line plus about €250M in upgrades to the existing route by 2034. The aim is under an hour between the cities; the full Bundestag vote looks like a formality.
“snake”, a 28-year-old Russian alleged to be a core member of the Qilin ransomware group, was arrested on holiday in Japan and extradited to Frankfurt (LKA NRW investigation).
DeepSeek is weighing doubling its funding round to as much as ¥100bn (~$14.9bn), with Tencent and CATL among the biggest backers and an IPO eyed for early 2027.
The FCC approved up to 15,000 SpaceX satellites for Starlink Mobile (direct-to-cell); Musk says V2 offers over 100× the bandwidth of V1.
Krebs: suspected ShinyHunters leader “Rey”, now detained in Jordan and reportedly cooperating with the FBI, was extorting Jeppesen ForeFlight (sold by Boeing) when he was picked up.
Chrome explains its JPEG XL support (decoding since Chrome 155): 30–50% better compression than JPEG, lossless JPEG recompression, HDR, and a decoder rewritten in Rust (jxl-rs) for memory safety.
curl 8.23.0 ships early, on 14 Oct, with 22 CVE fixes, including CVE-2026-92392, only the project’s third HIGH since 2021. Details stay under embargo until release.

GitHub had another incident hitting Git operations, pull requests and Actions. Jack Ellis: “This is happening constantly”; ex-GitHub engineer Sam Lambert says that kind of growth arriving so fast is very hard to react to.
ArtCraft: Brandon Thomas released clean-room Rust remakes of seven Adobe apps, built with Claude Opus 5.5. PhotoCraft has 14.6k stars; it is alpha, and patents are an open question.

Meta and Sierra’s Personal Agent Protocol (with Shopify, Stripe, Walmart and others): OAuth-based sessions for agents dealing with businesses via web, MCP/OpenAPI or company agents. v0.1 spec due later this month.
Status pages this evening: elevated errors on platform.claude.com, and degraded Codex/Work mode at OpenAI.

Warriors: Kristaps Porziņģis is out indefinitely with an undisclosed health issue and didn’t travel to camp in Hawaii. Steve Kerr calls it “definitely concerning”; he has missed 90 games over two seasons (POTS diagnosis in 2025).
BVB coach Niko Kovac calls the four-game international window “totally unacceptable” for clubs, after weeks without about 20 players. He would prefer three windows of two games.
